reviews.text:
In a toxic relationship with Honeybook. At first, HoneyBook was everything I needed. I could send invoices, collect signatures, schedule payments, capture leads, communicate with clients, receive payments, and keep my books organized all in one place. It felt like the perfect solution for my business.

But lately, our relationship has become toxic...

Simple tasks have become frustratingly difficult. I can’t reliably open or publish invoices. Sending emails is a gamble because they can sit loading for hours, sometimes days. Emails also randomly generate strange script, dashes, and special characters that make my messages look unprofessional.

The most frustrating part is that I know how good HoneyBook used to be. That’s what’s keeping me here. I keep hoping things will improve because when it worked, it worked really well.

Right now, though, I’m seriously considering other options. Especially for how much I am being charged each month. I need software that helps me run my business, not software that creates more work and stress. If HoneyBook can fix these performance and reliability issues, I’d love to stay. But at the moment, it feels like I’m holding onto what the relationship used to be instead of what it is now.

Mobile app needs better integration. The HoneyBook web app is the only way to really get work done. The mobile app is not full featured, and should be looked at as a companion only for basic check ins and replying to emails. There are quite a few things on mobile that make the experience disappointing. 

Ex. 1 - You’ve set an automation in the web app, and need to change it while out of the office. You can’t even see automation in the mobile app, so now you have to set a reminder to do it later when on the fully featured browser app and hopefully your client doesn’t get an email in the meantime from the automation workflow that they shouldn’t. The only option to remove automation in mobile is to archive. Not a good solution. 

Ex. 2 - you’ve set up a new project after an inquiry, and a potential client replies to an email from your automation. You go in to look for the project, but all you have is the client’s name from the email, and not the project name. You’re also out of luck, because your contacts don’t show links to projects in the mobile app like they do on the web app. 

The mobile app isn’t useless, but it’s limiting vs. the web app. That leaves me wondering why the mobile app isn’t addressed as a totally different platform, because it very much is. 

FYI, if I could get the same functionality from the web app in a mobile browser (phone or tablet), that would be a workaround I can live with. But the mobile browser version of HoneyBook is just as limited as the mobile app, so here we are.

reviews.text: HoneyBook-A Game Changer. HoneyBook makes my business processes run smooth. It has really change how I run my business and definitely gives me my time back.

Great Platform …with a few cons. I love what HB offers! It allows me to efficiently interact with my copywriting clients & they appreciate the all in one, easy to navigate propsal, contract signing & payment process. The client user experience has been great, but mine has been a bit rocky. 

The cons of HB for me are:
1) it was hard to learn & navigate
2) it’s pricey
3) doesn’t save emails as a draft which really sucked. 

Here’s what happened. On a couple of occasions while composing a message, I needed to go back & check the proposal, when I came back, all that I had written was gone! And I had written & edited quite a bit! 

Over all, a beautiful platform with great features it’s just not as intuitive and at times can frustrate me, even after 2 years.

Makes professionalism easy!. HoneyBook has been the best CRM I’ve used since starting my business. It makes everything so easy and seamless. My clients love it and I love that I can easily keep up with communications, documents, and more for my clients’ projects all in one tool.
